;Armed conflicts and attacks
*[[War in Afghanistan (2001–present)|War in Afghanistan]], [[Afghan peace process]], [[May 2020 Afghanistan attacks]]
**In the first attack since the end of a [[truce]] declared by the [[Taliban]], and despite a petition of the [[government of Afghanistan|government]] for the Taliban to extend the [[ceasefire]], at least 14 security forces members are killed in an attack on a [[security checkpoint|checkpoint]] in [[Parwan Province|Parwan]]. A government spokesperson says the Taliban also suffered casualties. The group has not commented on the attack. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2020/05/afghan-forces-killed-attack-blamed-taliban-200528084958150.html (Al Jazeera)]
*[[Rwandan genocide]]
**A court in [[Rwanda]] sentences former Mayor of Nyakizu [[Ladislas Ntaganzwa]] to [[life imprisonment]] for his role in orchestrating the [[massacre]] of hundreds of thousands of people in the 1994 [[genocide]]. His lawyer is planning to appeal the ruling. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2020/05/mayor-rwanda-sentenced-life-role-1994-genocide-200528153505555.html (Al Jazeera)]
*[[Somali Civil War (2009–present)|Somali Civil War]]
**Gunmen [[kidnapping|abduct]] multiple [[healthcare worker]]s in [[Balad District, Somalia|Balad]], [[Middle Shabelle]], before killing seven of them and another civilian. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-somalia-security/seven-health-workers-civilian-killed-in-somali-village-aid-group-idUSKBN2343DV (Reuters)]
*[[Herder–farmer conflicts in Nigeria]]
**Gunmen [[list of massacres in Nigeria|kill]] 60 to 74 people in villages in the [[Nigeria]]n [[states of Nigeria|state]] of [[Sokoto State|Sokoto]], where similar attacks had occurred on Monday. [https://www.bbc.com/pidgin/media-52830860 (BBC News)] [http://saharareporters.com/2020/05/28/update-death-toll-sokoto-gunmen-attack-rises-74 (SR)]

**[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United States]]
***The death toll from [[Coronavirus disease 2019|COVID-19]] in the [[United States]] exceeds 100,000. [https://edition.cnn.com/2020/05/27/politics/100000-deaths-moment-of-reflection/index.html (CNN)]

;International relations
*[[2020 China–India skirmishes]], [[China–India relations]]
**[[China]] moves thousands of [[People's Liberation Army]] troops to its [[Himalaya]]n [[Line of Actual Control|border with India]], bringing vehicles and heavy machinery to what [[India]] says is its territory. India sends several [[battalions]] of its [[Indian Army|Army]] from nearby [[Leh]] to the border in response. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2020/may/27/china-and-india-move-troops-as-border-tensions-escalate (''The Guardian'')]

;Law and crime
*[[George Floyd protests]]
**[[Killing of George Floyd]], [[George Floyd protests in Minnesota]]
***Protests continue for a second day in [[Minneapolis]] and other [[United States|U.S.]] cities after an unarmed man, [[George Floyd]], died while being arrested. Some of them have escalated into [[riot]]s, including [[looting]] and [[arson]]. [https://edition.cnn.com/2020/05/28/us/minneapolis-george-floyd-thursday/index.html (CNN)]
***A [[Minneapolis Police Department]] station is abandoned by police after being overran by protesters and is then looted and set on fire. An MPD spokesman confirmed the Third Precinct building had been evacuated "in the interest of the safety of our personnel". [https://www.politico.com/news/2020/05/29/minneapolis-police-protest-george-floyd-288361 (''Politico'')]
*[[COVID-19 pandemic in Malawi]], [[COVID-19 pandemic in Zimbabwe]]
**A manhunt is launched after hundreds of people, some with [[Coronavirus disease 2019|COVID-19]], escape from [[quarantine]] centers in [[Zimbabwe]] and [[Malawi]], with authorities worried that they will spread COVID-19 in countries whose health systems can be rapidly overwhelmed. [https://apnews.com/25e117c6c44f60d86375ff3ad3209468 (AP News)]

;Sports
*[[Impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on sports]], [[COVID-19 pandemic in Massachusetts]]
**The [[2020 Boston Marathon]] is officially canceled due to the COVID-19 pandemic. It is the first time in the event's 123-year history that the annual running had to be canceled. A modified version of the race, scheduled for September 14, will be run virtually, and runners who complete the marathon track in six hours or less will be eligible for the [[2021 Boston Marathon]]. [https://www.espn.com/olympics/trackandfield/story/_/id/29235688/boston-marathon-canceled-first-due-coronavirus (ESPN)]
